Cradle the sun

by Lilliae

Summary

“Just give me… some time and—and I can… change back. You don’t have to…”

Nothing more escaped him. Even that was too much for Phainon, lips pressed into a thin line mired with regret that he had spoken at all.

“I don’t have to what?”

Phainon didn’t answer.

“I don’t have to what, Phainon?” Mydei demanded, sharp and rough, but that was always when Phainon met him head on.

The truth spilled out in a cracked whisper. “Try and love me. When I—when I’m like this.”

Amphoreus’ first solar eclipse was meant to be a time for celebration. But the sight of daylight devoured by darkness dredges Phainon’s old memories and transformations with them in a frenzied haze.

Mydei proves to Phainon that his appearances, and the past entangled within them, has never mattered to him.

Notes

I would like to thank Hoyo for handing me on a silver platter the motivation to write another idea for this one shot series. This had been sitting in my drafts for months because I kept getting side tracked. I literally stopped writing out a long fic for this.

See the end of the work for more notes

chapters.title: Cradle the sun
chapters.html:
There was a nostalgia to the Chrysos Heirs gathered together in the Hero’s Bath. Their last meeting with full attendance, Nameless excluded since they had long journeyed elsewhere, had been a year and a half ago: a time of celebration, delayed a few months after Irontomb’s defeat and Amphoreus’ manifestation as a real planet. 

Since then there had been many meetings to discuss Amphoreus’ future. The situation was complex and demanded strategies for resettlement now that the black tide had receded and returned the land, damaged as it was, to the people.

Strategies for intergalactic negotiations, with the Nameless as mediators, to maintain Amphoreus’ autonomy when every power was itching to get their hands on it. Brute force, something Phainon provided in plenty, was sufficient but diplomacy was better at the beginning of their existence outside lines of code. 

Strategies for when exactly the Chrysos Heirs would step away from power. Unsurprisingly, after more than thirty-three million cycles of sacrifice, they were ready to relinquishes authority over the people and enjoy the more peaceful lives they had fought so hard for. 

“Castorice is being too modest,” Hyacine insisted, hair tied into bunches atop her head. “She’s been an invaluable assistant. And is growing into a capable physician in her own right.” 

With his elbows hooked over the bath edge, Mydei sipped his chalice of pomegranate juice. Leaned against his side, Phainon’s tipped his head back and Mydei lifted the chalice for him to take a sip before they both seamlessly returned to their own conversations. Personally, Mydei was observing more than partaking in the chatter. 

The colour in Castorice’s cheeks had little to do with the heat of the baths as she bashfully argued, “Only because I have a very capable teacher willing to help me.” 

Hyacine all but launched herself at Castorice, golden waters sloshing as she threw both arms over her shoulders in a side hug. Castorice stumbled and bumped the bath walls with a splash but returned the hold with more ease than once imaginable back when her touch brought Death. 

“My my, Princess Homebody has really grown out of her shell,” Cipher purred from her lounger by the bathside, chalice of wind in hand and fish platter on her lap. “What about little old me? Where’s my hug?” 

“Perhaps if the kitten fish ever outgrows her fears of the water,” Hysilens remarked without malice, eyes closed as she sat submerged to her chin. 

“Not all of us are little fishies who belong in the water,” Cipher snarked back with a flash of her fangs and claws. “Some of us belong on dry land and eat little fishies instead.” 

Cerydra huffed. “It would be a crime to even entertain the idea of eating such a beautiful fish. The only fitting punishment is to bow before the Dux Gladiorum and Imperator and beg for anything other than death.” 

“Aglaea,” Anaxa interrupted, “control your cat. If you insist we gather here, I would rather not be involved in something as juvenile as a water fight.” 

“Feel free to leave whenever you wish. The doors may not always be open for you to enter but the same cannot be said for your exit,” Aglaea retorted breezily. 

Despite coming to agreement many times over across the cycles, the two of them continued to squabble over the most benign topics. Yet, when it came to the value of Anaxa joining the Intelligentsia Guild or Aglaea setting a timeline to re-establish Okhema’s democratic processes, they were in perfect agreement. 

At least it was less awkward to bear witness to their provocations when Mydei was certain they had grown to be lighthearted. It was almost similar to him and Phainon. 

Except for the stickiness. Even now, Phainon was near plastered to Mydei’s side. He had snuck himself under Mydei’s arm, forcing it across Phainon’s shoulder, while a hand grabbed at Mydei’s waist. There was hardly space for steam nor water between them, even as the position forced Phainon to swivel his head right around to speak to Cyrene at his side. 

With the stature of a child finally growing into adulthood, Cyrene’s subdued smile was ill-fitting on her rounded face. “It reminds me of Aedes Elysiae. It’s still a small settlement for now but it has the potential to grow. The soil is most suitable for wheat, and it’s right beside the coast so the scent of the sea always breezes overhead.”

“It’s so peaceful there!” Tribios added with an excited kick of her feet as she sat a floating lounger, almost sitting herself adrift in Trinon hadn’t grabbed hold. 

It had been Cyrene and the triplets who volunteered to lead the resettlement programmes through the wilds of Amphoreus. It meant they spent a lot of time away from Okhema but the others occasionally joined them: Hysilens for a visit to the sea that was meaningful to more than herself, Anaxa to search for any lingering effects of the black tide that may have actualised with the rest of Amphoreus, and Phainon to accompany his childhood best friend he had been separated from for so long. 

Phainon smiled, bittersweet but hopeful. “It sounds incredible.” He turned to Mydei, hand squeezing his waist. “We should go.”

There was a stray stand of hair stuck to Phainon’s forehead and Mydei pushed it back before he answered, “I’ll make some time.”

It would require scheduling long in advance. Cerydra, Aglaea and himself had the most experience with the trappings of governance—negotiations, foresight, balancing the intersection between the security of the past, instability of the present, and uncertainty of the future. Bureaucracy too; although Mydei had less experience there than the other two—so they spent the most time intricately planning Amphoreus’ path into the future. Not to mention how his time was divided between Castrum Kremnos and Okhema. 

Phainon knew it was visit reserved for the distant future but he beamed and pecked Mydei’s cheek. 

Cipher gagged. “Oh lover boys, don’t get too caught up in each other’s eyes or you’ll miss the real show.”

Trianne gasped. “It’s starting!”

Through the open columns surrounding the Hero’s Bath, they were privy to a sweeping view of Okhema’s skyline. The rainbows Kephale wound around the city with Aquila’s aid, the mountaintops, the beautifully clear skies. Blue that became tinged dark, akin to black ink bleeding across the watery horizon. Not simply the gloom of a cloudy day, forewarning billowing winds and torrential rains, but something beyond those muted greys as the world itself dimmed. 

The sun was devoured by darkness and the sky blackened. 

An alignment of the sun and moon, restored in their fully glory to Amphoreus’ skies where they would remain for longer than the beginnings of a cycle. A solar eclipse. 

Mydei had witnessed partial ones in the past. From the walls of Castrum Kremnos, from the wilds of Amphoreus, even from the streets of Okhema. Different places at different times but all fleeting moments plagued with worry that the sun would never again emerge. That the black tide had drowned out the celestial bodies in an abyssal evernight. 

This was the first time he could recline in a warm bath with his closest companions, chalice of pomegranate juice in one hand and the other intertwined with Phainon’s hung over his shoulder, and simply enjoy the view. 

At first a mere crescent of darkness at the edge, the moon’s shadow rolled across the sun. Only the thinnest edge of the sun remained in a brilliant white. A starless daytime descended as the sun and moon devoured each other so day became night.

Cheers and laughter emanated from the Hero’s Bath in conjunction with those rising from the baths below. 

In Mydei’s hand, Phainon’s fingers twitched. 

“Everyone out the bath!”

Mydei didn’t know why the command rumbled from deep in his chest in a tone reserved for life and death on the battlefield. But his mind and body were trained to react. To sense danger before it could strike him dead. His instincts were scarcely wrong. 

He lunged through waters dragging him backwards and yanked Trinnon into the air. She yelped but there was no time to apologise as he tossed her with one hand onto a nearby kline while the other snatched up Trianne to do the same. He whirled around in search of anyone else but the others had all scrambled out at his warning cry. 

Just in time for the golden waters to erupt. 

A scorching heat melted Mydei’s skin, sloughing flesh from his bones and charring white to black as the water boiled into steam in an instant. It superheated him, air popping in his lungs as it expanded and burst from his chest. 

All things considered, it was a quick death. More sudden and less painful than Dawnmaker through his tenth thoracic vertebra at the tail end of a lengthy struggle. It was a brief moment where the world vanished from his eyes and then he gasped back to life. 

The bath tiles were still hot under his new skin as he rolled off his back and clambered to his feet. The bath was completely dry.  

The healing glow faded from Hyacine’s hands. “Mydei! You’re back already.”

She grabbed onto one arm while Castorice grasped the other, helping him balance while lightheaded from a sudden death and revival. They guided him towards the bath edge and Hysilens offered a hand to pull him out. 

A dark sky overhead. The crescent opening as the sun and moon began to part ways once again. Not much time had passed but Mydei catalogued the heirs for injuries and—

“Phainon?” he croaked out, throat still raw from the blast of steam. 

Despite the troubled pinch above her clear eyes, Aglaea’s maintained her composure as she explained, “He used the power of the Coreflames to assume that transformed state.”

Cipher’s playful lilt had vanished, tail lashing behind her. “If I had to gamble, I would say he flew off to Dawncloud.”

Mydei waved off Hyacine and Castorice’s concern, the two of them sharing a look and Hyacine a final burst of healing light, re-energising him, before relinquishing their hold. 

He nodded at them in thanks. “I’ll go after him.”

Cyrene gazed at the sky in search of a new star. When she failed to find it, she turned to Mydei with grim determination and hope. “Good luck.”

The power of Strife left to slumber within him in this time of hard-fought peace was suddenly stirred awake. For one moment it remained a sluggish trickle but, like a lion yawning as it roused from slumber, it forewarned the awakened energy that burst through him all at once. 

It wasn’t a spear he summoned, nor did he brandish a sword resonating with the souls of deceased warriors. The wings of Fury burst from his back in six weighted segments that settled, new yet familiar, an extension of himself, and he soared into the brightening sky. 

When Kephale shouldered the Dawn Device, they naturally replaced the sun that had once shone over Okhema. At the city’s heart, where the people gathered to decide all matters of daily life, the true sun was gone from sight and those who usually lingered around the assembly had flocked elsewhere to better witness the rare celestial event. 

Dawncloud was deserted. There was no one else to gaze upon the blazing sun come down to earth. Only Mydei. 

Phainon and the Trailblazer had mentioned this transformation in the past—in passing. The only times Mydei had witnessed it for himself were those final duels that set the remains of his life ablaze for the sake of deliverance into the next cycle. They were fast, frantic, heart and mind racing to surpass all expectations knowing Phainon would best him anyway. It was a show of respect, a test of resolve, and Phainon was never one to fail him. 

This transformation was a sight accompanied by the clash between Strife and the Worldbearer at their pinnacle. When the Lance of Fury was poised to strike Dawnmaker and the very air burned with the sparks while blood and dust obscured black and gold. 

In the absence of battle, this was the first time Mydei could see Phainon. 

Two wings extended from his back with feathers as worn and weary as the hunched shoulders that carried them. The heat had scorched his clothes to ash, exposing skin paler than usual that basked in none of the golden warmth bleeding from jagged cracks. Dawnmaker’s corroded edge hung at his side. 

Mydei’s wings folded upon themselves and disappeared. They thrummed where Strife slumbered beneath the surface for him to call upon. His bare feet landed silently on the ground. 

Phainon had always been adept at sensing his presence. Not by sight, by scent or by sound. Once, more than once but always the first in the memory of that Mydei, he had tested which one was the cause behind Phainon’s head perking up and finding him the moment he was nearby. He had systemically eliminated each one but the results were unchanged. 

Yet Phainon was unmoved. Wings still, head bowed. The only movement was the gold swirling beneath the skin. 

When no acknowledgement came, Mydei approached on steps louder than usual in the hopes of alerting Phainon to his presence. That shadowed spot on the ground he was so enraptured by—Mydei was certain he had died there once. It would be more difficult to find somewhere in the streets of Okhema or Castrum Kremnos where he hadn’t perished. 

“… Dawn Device…” Phainon croaked through a hoarse throat. “… black tide…” 

He muttered more to himself, incomprehensible, and grasped at his face. The Dawn Device was extinguished, as it had been since the black tide receded and the natural daylight cycle restored. 

But that wasn’t what Phainon remembered. 

Nothing remained of the relaxed smile Phainon had relearned to let himself ease into over the past year. None of the fondness Phainon had always shown Mydei and they were never allowed to keep for themselves until now. Only the wild eyes and bared lips in the snarl of a desperate, wounded animal. 

“… your Coreflame…” 

Mydei dropped. His fist slammed into the ground and red crystals burst from the cracks in his skin and the earth. His muscles spasmed with the effort. Unused. Forgotten. Far from the casual spars that were more play fighting, rough housing and teasing than real training.

It was passable effort and intercepted Dawnmaker’s slash aimed at his neck. 

He dragged his fingertips across the ground and an arc of crystal burst forth. A barrier. Cover, as he changed position. 

It crumbled in two slices but it was enough time for Mydei to prepare. More crystals sprouted from the stone and snagged Dawnmarker’s tip in their craggy grasp. Phainon would break it with ease but that brief moment of confusion, weapon and arm catching, let Mydei ram his elbow into Phainon’s wrist. Fingers spasmed and dropped Dawnmaker into the maws of the red beast devouring it whole.  

That levelled the battlefield somewhat. Mydei was still in his bath robe; no shoes, no gauntlets, no spear. If Castrum Kremnos’ Blade of Fury suddenly swung towards Okhema, or the Lance of Fury anppeared over Dawncloud like an executioner’s sword, it would be a troublesome mess to clean up. For him as well as Aglaea and Cerydra. 

This was more familiar as they circled one another. Hands empty and twitching with the urge to grapple. It would minimise the damage. To their surroundings and each other. 

When Amphoreus became real, the Heirs had ascended to the status of the Titans mythologised in the minds of the people. The same as Aglaea’s blindness, Castorice’s embrace of Death, and Cyrene’s body frozen in time, Mydei’s immortality had changed. The power remained but had shed its flaws. 

As the embodiment of Strife, his body was still far from fragile and had lost the only weakness it once had. But he knew the face Phainon would make once he came back to his senses and saw the damage he had inflicted. If that involved a sword through Mydei’s back, Phainon would never trust himself again. 

Phainon’s eyes glowed in the low light of the eclipse—the sun plucked from the sky and claimed as his own. Now searing its way out of him to pierce through Mydei without seeing him. All instinct and no thought. 

He knew exactly how many times Phainon had killed him. A number he didn’t care for but had ticked up, up, up until the act was engrained in Phainon’s body. Unwavering as it speared his blade through Mydei’s tenth thoracic vertebra. The same way Phainon could pick him from a crowd in an instant, Dawnmaker could find his weak spot blind. 

Mydei struck first. A jab at Phainon’s nose to try and rattle some sense back into his brain. He reared away, a smooth dodge, and swiped for Mydei’s forearm. He crooked his arm, snapping his weight at the waist, and smacked Phainon’s hand away with his elbow. The momentum carried into the sweep of his leg into Phainon’s side. 

The kick sent him sprawling. Mydei held back enough to keep his ribs intact but he should have slammed into the assembly’s seats. His wings opened to catch the wind, slowing him to a graceful stop where he hovered, upright and unfazed. 

The end feathers curled. No time for any meagre defensive walls, Mydei lowered his weight and braced. 

Not enough. Phainon launched at him with a beat of his wings that crossed the assembly in a blink. A comet blazing towards him and Mydei grappled at his arms, his shoulders, with hands that seared others now scorched by Phainon’s heat.

If only he had shoes for traction, there may have been a chance of staying on his feet. Without them, his toes gripped at loosened stone. They sliced through the thin skin, slicking his soles with blood that took his feet out from under him. 

Mydei hit the ground first. He was accustomed to fighting, to falling, and braced against the collision. He was unwinded, hold steady, and he retaliated with a jab at Phainon’s throat. It was a mess of flailing limbs. Swing, block, jab. Find an advantage. Make one. 

With the scant distance between them, the air tasted of smoke and ash. The embers settled in his lungs as he panted, head lurching away as Phainon’s armoured fist smashed through the stone in place of his skull. The more he breathed, the more the air sparked the flames crackling in his chest. Throat coarse, eyes so dry they could no longer water, the flames soaring up his lungs to his racing heart. 

He smacked Phainon’s fist out from under him. Off-balance, he went easily as Mydei wrapped his legs around his waist, arms around his neck, and rolled them. He was still underneath when he stopped them but he had Phainon locked in a secure hold by the neck. 

Ragged wings thrashed but the tattered feathers were soft even as they beat arid, desert winds into Mydei’s face that were nothing compared to the scorch where their bare skin met. 

Did Phainon need to breathe in this form? Did he have lungs, a beating heart, where the coronal radiance from millions of Coreflames resided in his weathered chest? Mydei hoped so, otherwise the chokehold cutting off his airflow was useless. 

Both wings flared and Mydei winced as Phainon’s body temperature increased with a blinding flash piercing through brittle skin. He only tightened his hold. 

The sun had returned but a new shadow fell upon them. He knew what it was. 

He shoved Phainon away and scrambled to his feet, twisting on the way up so, no time to lose, he could sprint out of the blast zone. He vaulted over the assembly wall and tucked himself as he landed between the seats with his arms wrapped around his head and breath held in his tight chest. 

The first meteor fell. The collision rocked through him. Dust and stone plumed to block out the sun. The entirety of Dawn Cloud trembled and Mydei braced for his stomach to plummet with the sky island. 

The tremors subsided but the Destruction never demonstrated restraint. One strike was only the first of many. 

At this rate, the Dawn Device would be knocked from Kephale’s shoulders, Dawncloud would be grounded, and Okhema, with its busy streets of festivities, would be flattened while many parts of it were still under reconstruction. 

Amidst the dust and debris blotted with shadows falling from above, Mydei clambered to his feet, healed but raw against the rough stone, and extended a hand before him. The air crackled like lightning, like blood sizzling on the hot coals of war, and he grasped hold of it in the way reserved for the embodiment of Strife. 

Gold formed beneath his fingers. A polearm, extending on both sides. He grabbed hold of this extension of his body—both the wielder and the lance that felled armies and cities—and slammed the Lance of Fury into the ground. 

The spearhead towered upwards to pierce the sky in a thundering boom and flash of lighting that shattered meteors into fine rain. The dust dissipated. 

Red crystals littered the ground where Dawnmaker had once been trapped. Phainon was gone. 

Mydei twisted on instinct. Too slow. A weight, sturdy as iron yet heated molten, slammed into him. His head cracked against the seat. Light speckled across a dimmed, blurred world that was soon reduced to Phainon as they hit the floor. 

Phainon’s eerily black face above him. Phainon’s weight atop him, on his knees while a hand pinning Mydei by the chest. Phainon’s sword levelled at his torso where he could pierce through to that single notch in his spine. 

If the blade went clean through flesh and bone, Mydei would survive. Phainon would not. 

But his head was spinning and the world with it. His body was weak beneath the oppressive heat smothering him. His voice was almost beyond reach as he rasped, “Deliverer.”

At that, Phainon blinked. The pale skin of his face—reminiscent of glazed and fired pottery. A theatre mask painted in tragedy. So easy to shatter—pulled. Confusion in his parted lips that breathed for the first time since he burned himself up in panic over an end that had come and gone numerous times and never again. 

“You…” His eyes flicked across Mydei’s face. Frantic but seeing as his grip faltered around Dawnmaker. 

“The dawn arrived.” He reached up and wrapped his hand around Dawnmaker’s edge. He steadied it, trembling with Phainon’s hand, where it was poised to stab him through. “You brought us the dawn, Phainon.”

Dawnmaker slipped through Phainon’s fingers into Mydei’s awaiting hand. He tossed it aside and opened his arms in time for Phainon to collapse against him. Steadfast for so long, now Phainon was shaking all over, as though he had been frozen somewhere beneath the sun blazing in his chest and was only just beginning to thaw. Mydei wrapped his arms around him, tucking Phainon’s head beneath his chin, and held him through the worst of the tremors. 

He was excruciatingly hot. His skin blistered from every point of contact, heat branding itself in the shape of Phainon sprawled across him. Boiling water, flowing magma, clinging to him.

If only Mydei’s temperature was low enough to offer Phainon the briefest reprieve of cooling him down, but Mydei’s body had always thrummed hot. It dulled the edge, Mydei closer than anyone else to the heat Phainon had taken upon himself and endured, as Phainon cauterised them—wounds, scars, blood—together. 

“Phainon.”

Unresponsive. His shoulders rose and fell in quick, shallow breaths burning like glowing coals across Mydei’s clavicle, skin red and sweat pooled in his collarbones where it wasn’t allowed to cool. His muscles had stopped twitching except the occasional spasm in his fingers. There was no proper response; no sign Phainon had heard him.

The broken stones dug into Mydei’s back. They were exposed to the elements and anyone who came searching through the debris for the source of the chaos; although he doubted anyone would be brave enough for that. The middle of Dawncloud’s assembly was a less than ideal place to rest, especially when, head tipped back, he could see Kephale gazing down at them. 

Perhaps he had fainted but Mydei tapped the back of his neck anyway. “I’m taking us home.”

With their position and similar statures, it was awkward to manoeuvre Phainon into his arms so Mydei could climb to his feet. Phainon was limp, complete dead weight, in Mydei’s arms as he shuffled him into a bridal carry. Even his wings hung uselessly from his back while Mydei’s sprouted and lifted them into the air with a single powerful push.

He was accustomed to travelling much greater distances when he flew between Okhema and Castrum Kremnos. The journey gave him practice carrying Phainon, whenever he insisted on joining him, so it was with ease that he balanced their combined weight while he took off, swooped through the air, and soon landed again. 

With so many people on the streets, they must have seen the spectacle on Dawncloud. Then Mydei’s bright wings shooting across the city with Phainon in his arms. Together they glowed like a comet, a shooting star, a ray of sunlight splintered from the eclipsed sun. 

One of the boons from living near the city outskirts was that the streets around their home were quiet. Everyone had flocked to the widest streets and plazas for the festivities, leaving no one to witness Mydei prop Phainon up in one hand, like a particularly large sack of pomegranates, and jostle their front door open with the other.

Their home had never been so quiet. Not when the two of them were home together. There was always some kind of noise that came with living: crackling fire and sizzling oil in the kitchen, one half of a conversation over the teleslate, pages turning, pen scratching, playful arguments and laughter and conversations about what they had done today and would do tomorrow. 

But Phainon was silent as Mydei carried him through to the bedroom. His sharp breathes had evened out into something Mydei saw in the rise of his shoulders and felt against his exposed collarbone rather than heard. His wings had twitched into half an embrace, one draped over Mydei’s shoulder and the other over Phainon’s own, but they couldnt hide Phainon’s dazed face away completely. 

He lowered Phainon to the kline. Since his temperature was so high a blanket may not be of much comfort but Mydei grabbed the one folded over the kline’s curve and pooled it beside Phainon for him to decide. The closed curtains would be of far greater comfort, darkness cooler and easier on his eyes and head. Yet the thought of Phainon stuck in the dark made Mydei’s jaw clench.

“I’m leaving to get some water,” Mydei warned, whether Phainon could hear him or not. 

Whilst Castrum Kremnos was a warmongering city-state that espoused personal sacrifice for glory, ideology was easy to cry and difficult to follow. It wasn’t only new recruits that suffered from paralysis and waking nightmares. Veteran warriors had lost themselves to the same affliction of the mind. He had seen it for himself as a royal general and the leader of the detachment, as well as they ways comrades eased each other back to reality. 

It was a quick stop in the kitchen for two chalices and water kept cold in the icebox but he lingered in front of the andron doorway. The solar eclipse had ended and the sunlight returned in full, shining through the window warm rather than scorching. 

It had never been this bad before. Although Phainon’s carefree smile had returned, bringing with it a myriad of others that Mydei was welcome to more than others, there were moments. Slips of time where he forgot who he was, where he was, and the freedom that was finally theirs to claim.

Just never like this. A transformation Phainon had kept sequestered away for almost two years. A mind foggy of everything except an instinct to hunt and slaughter. Or maybe this had occurred before—in those early weeks following Irontomb’s fall when Phainon confined himself to solitude in a dark, stagnant room—and maybe Mydei simply hadn’t been privy to it. 

His portable teleslate had been left behind in Marmoreal Palace with his clothes but his drawing one was still where he had left it that morning. He had put it down with haste and much pestering on Phainon’s behalf, with remarks on his lacking sociability because he would rather draw on his teleslate than hurry to make the meeting with their friends. Mydei would never disrespect anyone else’s time by arriving late; something Phainon knew, yet he goaded him anyway and Mydei acquiesced in the end. 

There was a queue of notifications demanding his attention. He sent a quick update to the Chrysos Heir group. Then a slightly longer one shared between him, Aglaea and Cerydra with an apology for the damage done to Dawn Cloud they would need to draft a response to. The public was always in need of reassurance. The present and future were rife with uncertainty now that the true Era Nova splintered life away from millions of years living along the same cyclical tracks.

Then he took a deep breath and turned his back on the sun that embraced all life for the one that was Mydei’s alone to hold.

In his absence, Phainon had forgone the blanket. His wing sufficed where he was curled upon his side. The feathers twitched at Mydei approach, and then stilled when he stopped beside the kline to set the chalices upon the cabinet. 

“Phainon.” 

His outermost feathers furled. In some way, Phainon could hear him. He either couldn’t or refused to respond. 

The mattress dipped with Mydei’s weight as he sat. It rolled Phainon towards him. Just a little. Just enough for his hand to be exposed from beneath his wing and the metal band on his finger to gleam in the sunlight reaching for Phainon as though he didn’t burn bright enough on his own. 

Mydei curled his hand beneath Phainon’s fingertips. He tensed, muscles halfway to flinching back, but Mydei brushed his thumb along Phainon’s ring finger. 

“Can you feel this?” No verbal response but the temperature of Phainon’s hand oscillated between flashing hot and rapidly cooling. “What is it? Tell me.”

A shuddering breath. The raw rasp of his voice scraping out his parched throat, “Ring…”

Mydei’s lips threatened to curl into a smile but he knew better than to celebrate prematurely and he hummed, falling on the pleasant side of neutral. “Why do you have a ring?”

His wings fluttered, fingers curling into something that resembled a proper grip, and the light pulsed from his chest. “Because…” 

He struggled for anything more. Mydei waited, hand in Phainon’s and finger running steady lines across his ring finger. When Phainon couldn’t answer, hand and wings slackening, Mydei tried another angle of approach

Questions and physical touch were working. He just needed the right ones. 

“When did I give it to you? What time of day?”

He blinked twice in quick succession and Mydei belatedly realised Phainon hadn’t blinked until now. If his eyes were perpetually too dry to even water, he had no need to blink. “Dawn.”

That made Mydei relent to a smile and a quiet huff of laughter at the memory of it. The soft palette of the rising dawn had coloured Phainon’s hair a pale pink, the same hue as pomegranate juice mixed with goat’s milk, and warmed his pupils rose gold as they widened at the ring presented in Mydei’s hand. 

Now, he guided Phainon’s hand up, meeting no resistance as he murmured, “The true dawn.”

The ring was hot against his lips but couldn’t compare to Phainon’s skin as Mydei trailed kisses up to his fingertip, across to another and back down to his knuckles. Phainon sucked in a hissing breath but his hand was relaxed in Mydei’s own, against Mydei’s lips as he worked his way around to kiss the centre of his dry palm. Entrusted to him. 

He kissed Phainon’s callouses earned from years of dedicated swordsmanship. Phainon’s fingertips that had used that skill to cut Mydei open and bathe in gold. Phainon’s inner wrist where his blood pulsed to the same thundering rhythm as the light emanating from within. 

Phainon’s head was still but his eye strained at its corners to watch as Mydei pressed kisses into the veins up his arm, uncertain whether he would bleed gold or bleed sunlight but unwilling to see for himself when Phainon deserved so much more. 

Every brush of his lips was gentle against Phainon’s brittle skin. Anything more and this body held together by sheer will power against the erosion through millions of years may finally crumble to ash. 

The look in Phainon’s eyes was already halfway gone. Pupils large, eyes wide, they stared and stared and stared. Hazy disbelief. Confused uncertainty. Wild panic. 

“Stop.” 

Mydei stilled with his nose in the crook of Phainon’s elbow. He immediately backed away and searched for Phainon’s gaze. 

Phainon’s head was slack against the bedsheets, eyes shut so tight the corners that should have creased began to flake and crack. “Just give me… some time and—and I can… change back. You don’t have to…”

Nothing more escaped him. Even that was too much for Phainon, lips pressed into a thin line mired with regret that he had spoken at all. 

“I don’t have to what?” 

Phainon didn’t answer. 

But Phainon had made this equally about Mydei as about himself. He refused to accept his silence when Phainon was shrinking under the weight of a speech suppressed so the thoughts would plague him alone. 

“I don’t have to what, Phainon?” Mydei demanded, sharp and rough, but that was always when Phainon met him head on. 

The truth spilled out in a cracked whisper. “Try and love me. When I—when I’m like this.” 

It took a moment too long for Mydei to understand Phainon’s words. In that heavy silence, Phainon’s wings curled tighter around himself and his hand almost dropped from Mydei’s grasp. 

He refused to let go. “I’ve never needed to try.”

Feathers bristled, opening, despite his stubborn refusal to let Mydei in and see this aspect, one kept so carefully hidden until now, of the person Mydei had always come to cherish more than any other. 

Not always by choice. Sometimes it was a feeling he had smothered with the hopes it would pass. Because the fate of Amphoreus—the Kremnoans who looked to Mydei’s back. Phainon’s personal quest for revenge—came before any of their feelings that would only end in separation when Phainon, The Deliverer, alone witnessed the new beginning to come.   

More often than violence, his response was to nurture it. Quietly. For himself and for Phainon, who would receive the parts Mydei was willing to show him in their spars, their marketplace visits, their ridiculous competitions when he kept everyone else at arms length. But neither of them ever gave it a name. 

Then there were the times when their passion bled into reckless abandon. Amphoreus would end and a new one would begin, the tragedy they expected that came in an unexpected way, but they could indulge in each other for now. Despite how that love would turn to violence and destroy them both when the time came to part ways. 

Now that all those memories were his to keep hold of, he could smile with amusement at the things they had done, the people they had been, and self-deprecation at his own foolishness, knowing beyond doubt that: 

“I suffered far more in my attempts to not love you.”

Such futile endeavours when they were always going to end up here—sharing a home, a bed, as many lifetimes as they could carve out for themselves—even if fate disagreed and imposed itself upon them. 

In the silence, the hitch of Phainon’s breath echoed. The same way it rippled through him to the tips of his fingers and feathers. Phainon could obscure his eyes, his face, even most of his body, but he could never hide everything. Not from Mydei. Not when his every thought and emotion was as plain to see as the sunlight spilling from him, as the ink on Mydei’s own skin, as the rings upon each of their fingers. 

He laid another kiss against Phainon’s ring; a symbol of the vow they had taken many times over, yet incomparable to the one spoken on the cusp of endless tomorrows they could experience together. “Do you doubt me?”

“No.” It was the steadiest Phainon had sounded since before the sun was devoured from the sky.

“Then lay back.”

For a moment, Phainon was unmoved while Mydei continued to scatter kisses along the lines of his fingers, his knuckles, down the bones along the back of his hand. Then his wing lifted and he rolled onto his back. 

He glimpsed the stark contrast where pale skin met blackened armour but Phainon’s wings were quick to fold around him again. Unlike before, the wings curled around his body weren’t self-suffocating, self-immolating; it was a gentle embrace, seeking comfort in himself. 

His face was left exposed, feathers grazing his bottom lips and no higher. With Phainon patiently gazing up at him, eyes frightfully but innocently wide, Mydei couldn’t contain his smile. Like a startled chimera who yearned to be petted but didn’t dare ask. 

“No matter your name, your appearance—“ he leaned closer, hand bracing beside Phainon’s head while the other cupped his cheek to caress skin one harsh move away from fracturing. If it did, Mydei would hold and kiss him the same, “—to me you’ve never changed.”

Tattered feathers tickled his chin as he closed the final distance and pressed their lips together. Pressure almost nonexistent, pace languid. Phainon’s lips were dry where they moved against his: timid but wanting. Mydei coaxed him to show their usual fervour, so greedy, so all-consuming, it was a selfishness Phainon reserved for him and Mydei wanted him to be selfish. 

Even as Phainon’s hands remained fisted in the sheets, Phainon’s wings parted and slipped beneath Mydei’s arms to wrap around the both of them. Wanting to be close, to hold and be held, despite how he denied himself. 

Mydei pulled away, lungs scorching with Phainon’s breath in them and lips tingling from the heat. It was a pleasant burn, nothing to fear or shy away from; he sought it out against the corner of Phainon’s lips, the swell of his cheeks, the tip of his nose—everywhere Mydei could think to leave kisses like light rain on sun-baked stone. 

Words should never be used where actions sufficed. It was a Kremnoan creed and one Phainon had come to understand because Mydei was well-versed in the words that mattered but it was actions that harboured most of his care. So Phainon laid still beneath him as Mydei pressed the truth, of his care, of his affections, deeper than skin and a sun capable of cleansing the universe. 

He trailed kissed down Phainon’s neck, dipping into his collarbones where the cracks began to form. Gold simmered underneath and burst in gold protrusions. Mydei’s finger dragged along the sharp edges before he skimmed his way across the gold line cut across his clavicle to his other shoulder. 

The skin had hardened to a burnt husk but it was still smooth beneath Mydei’s lips as he worked his way down Phainon’s arm to lavish it with the same attention he had earlier given the other. He kissed the crook of his elbow, traced a golden vein showing through the black down to his wrist, and followed his palm up to his fingers, back down, and across to the next. His fingertips, his nails, his knuckles. 

Up again. His wrist, his upper arm, his shoulder. Only to go down his chest where the cracks were largest and the heat most intense. His brow prickled with the beginnings of perspiration as his finger skimmed the jagged edges of Phainon’s chest and his lips followed. 

This close, the searing heat was akin to standing in front of a forge, laying in a drought-ridden field with no shade in sight, setting the flames of Strife and Destruction and basking in the agonising radiance that destroyed everything except them. 

Down his tapered waist and past his thigh. Short, chaste kisses against Phainon’s knee, his shin, all the way to the knob of his inner ankle. Then he retraced his path back up so he could descend the lines of Phainon’s other leg. 

Phainon allowed it. Whenever Mydei glanced up through his lashes, Phainon watched with heady eyes caught between capturing every moment and glancing away in embarrassment. His chest rose and fell in short, sharp breaths but it was nothing like the frenzy of his hazy mind seeing the peaceful city as a battlefield. 

Mydei met his eye, smirk crooking his lips, and dared him to look away as he climbed back up his body. It had cooled somewhat by the time he returned to meet Phainon halfway for a kiss. 

This time, Phainon led—the tilt of his head, the press of his lips, the arms wrapped around the back of his neck—and Mydei was more than happy to succumb to his rhythm. Whatever Phainon wanted to give him, to take from him, because they were the same and their answer would always be everything. 

By the time Phainon let Mydei back away, the light within his chest had dimmed into something scarce. Dark like the sea depths where it had once been radiant gold, yet still emitting a low light. 

The skin of his cheek beneath Mydei’s thumb was no longer brittle pottery but worn paper, thin and grainy. It had already torn and opened chasms across Phainon’s cheek, his nose bridge, and converged in a gaping crack, splitting him open from his missing eye to the crown of his head. 

His remaining eye peered up at him and the white flames, burning without emitting much light, all of it cold in hue yet scalding enough for sweat to bead along Mydei’s forehead, flickered with his uncertainty. Mydei raised a hand and paused for any objections. When none came, he ran his hand through Phainon’s hair. 

It was white again but had lost its lustre and fluffiness. It was flat and brittle, coarse and hollow, even before Mydei brushed the ones closest to the crack and glanced inside to the flames lying low inside. Weak. 

Phainon had burned himself out. His mind, his body. From one form to the next. He was still Phainon and Mydei kissed his forehead, below the crack across his nose, and finally his lips. 

He was larger like this. Taller, broader, despite the obvious fragility when his breaths whistled in and out all the holes eroded through him. As though the hot air and smoke from the dying flames swirling within him had stretched his paper-thin body to the limit.

Still Phainon. Always. Through every cycle, he never changed. That self-sacrificial nature, that immeasurable strength of will, that hatred he could cultivate alongside all the love threatening to burst from his heart. 

The tears scarcely touched the crease of his hazy, unfocused eye before it dissipated with the hiss of steam. Mydei dragged his thumb there, as though there were still tears to gather, because he knew Phainon had more to shed, and then left a small kiss in place of tears. 

Everywhere Mydei had left a soft touch or tender kiss received another as he made his way down Phainon’s body. His neck, his shoulders, his arms. The lines and folds of his hands and his fingers. The cracks in his chest that had grown as his body temperature cooled. The swell of his thighs, his knobbly knees, the soles of his feet. 

These forms Phainon had inhabited for so long and experienced nothing but derision would receive the love they had deserved all along. 

And he knew Phainon finally felt it when he cupped the back of Mydei’s neck and coaxed him down for a kiss. Every drop of adoration Mydei had given him was returned. Shared. Neither of them gaining nor losing. It ran hot down the back of Mydei’s throat and settled in his chest with the gentle warmth of the hearth welcoming him home. 

He opened his eyes to endless blue staring back. Not quite as bright as usual but lightening like the sky after a storm had come and gone, upending things in its wake but it was far from total destruction, annihilation. It was just a minor mess; simple to deal with, and Mydei savoured the opportunity. 

The skin of Phainon’s chest was more supple, regaining colour as it stretched over the gaps in his chest and head. The same pink flush of life had begun to bloom across his lips when Phainon dragged him back down for another kiss. Another, and another, as his body stitched itself back together—healing—until Mydei’s palm could feel soft skin over taut muscle, and the heart beating steady underneath. 

“Hi,” Phainon breathed when he next drew away for air he once again needed, smile woozy with affection shining through the exhaustion. “I’m back.”

Mydei huffed a laugh but placed a kiss against Phainon nose just to watch it wrinkle without skin breaking. “You never left. Now have some water.”

Phainon pouted despite the lingering rasp in his voice, “So those other forms get lots of kisses, and this one gets some water? At this rate, I’ll start to think you like those appearances more than this one.” 

“They were quieter.” 

Phainon let out a scandalised gasp, tapering off into a wheeze. “My voice is one of my best assets.” 

“Then drink some water before you lose it.” 

Phainon’s pout deepened but the crinkle at his eyes, skin that creased instead of cracked, betrayed his joy as Mydei guided him upright with a hand at his back. The two chalices of water were slightly above room temperature but they had survived better than the scorched sheets, and the warmth was better for Phainon’s strained vocal cords. 

He cleared his throat, voice coming clean of grit and ash when he said, “There we go. Now I can seduce you properly.” 

Mydei rolled his eyes. “It’s as I told you before: I’ve never needed to try. And neither have you.” 

Phainon’s lips flapped uselessly around some empty words before it settled into a resigned smile, one that found delight in defeat, as his cheeks flushed. “Yeah.” His smile softened still, thumb caressing Mydei’s bottom lip, damp with water yet the dryness persisted. “Your lips are sore.”

“Cease your worrying. It will heal.”

A non-committal hum as Phainon pushed his lips down, exposing his teeth. Mydei’s questioning, flat stare was answered by Phainon’s fingers moving to hook his chin and tug him into another kiss. Apologetic and sweet. Refreshingly cool against Mydei’s burns. 

Even his balmy breath was a reprieve as Phainon opened a scant distance between them, eyes half-closed as he murmured, “Let’s watch the sunrise tomorrow.”

“It’s a date,” Mydei promised and sealed it with a kiss against his forehead, soft white bangs tickling his nose. “For now, we both need a bath.”

Mydei more so than Phainon. The sheer heat of his body had warded off most the dirt while Mydei’s skin and hair were tainted with it. 

Phainon tipped his head in confusion and frowned. “Did I…”

“Our own will have to suffice,” Mydei confirmed. 

After all, Phainon had evaporated all the water in the Hero’s Bath. 

He dropped his head into his hands with a groan. “I’ll apologise to everyone tomorrow.” His brows furrowed, frown deepening. “I ruined the celebration.”

“You can repent by helping plan and prepare the next one,” Mydei quashed his worries before they could fester. 

At their plans for the future, Phainon’s mood lifted. “And I know how to make it up to you, too.”

Mydei sighed, “That’s—“

Unnecessary was swept away from him as quickly as Phainon swept him off the mattress and into his arms. It was much less dramatic when he needed to awkwardly shuffle on his knees to the edge of the kline before standing. 

Mydei swiftly resigned himself to his fate of being carried in Phainon’s sturdy arms and looped his own around Phainon’s neck while he walked them to the bathroom. He set Mydei on the bath stool while he lit the furnace to boil the water, and returned with the hair comb, jars of oil and ash, the pumice stone, and the strigil. While Phainon mixed the oil and ash, Mydei stripped out the torn and scorched remains of his bath robe then sat back down. 

All the delicate care Mydei had lavished upon Phainon was reflected in Phainon’s diligent doting as he brushed the dirt from Mydei’s hair with a mix of the comb and his fingers. Once the major debris was gone, he tied it back so Mydei could wet it when he was ready. 

Then he lathered the oil and ash upon Mydei’s body. He started with one arm, massaging the mixture into his skin as though Mydei wouldn’t realise he was searching for injuries they both knew would be long healed by now. 

Stood between Mydei’s legs, it was easy to see the exhaustion weighty in the lines of Phainon’s face, dipped forwards and lashes lowered to narrow his attention on his handiwork. It was the same level of dedication artisans bestowed upon their best masterpieces. 

Once he was satisfied, he took the strigil and scraped the mixture off into a bucket. He ran his thumb along the flickering lines of Mydei’s tattoos, checking for any speck of dirt, ash or oil left behind. Then he skimmed across his shoulders, thumb pausing in the centre of the mark of Strife, before continuing with his other arm.

His arm, his chest, his back. Phainon even dropped to his knees and cleaned off Mydei’s legs one after the other. His fingers traced the rises and dips of honed muscle, and where they intersected with his tattoos with the purest appreciation. The overwhelming care was so palpable he could taste it, near suffocating him with something other than pure heat but just as deadly, and knew it was the same he had given Phainon.

As Phainon lowered Mydei into the heated bath water blooming with the scent of hyacinths, as though those three steps were too far for Mydei to be allowed to walk on his own feet, and Phainon took a moment to pillow his arms on the washbasin and gaze at him with a small, sincere smile, he belatedly realised there was only one word for it. Reverence. 

“Which is your best?” Mydei asked out of some vague curiosity. 

Phainon shuffled at Mydei’s back and curled an arm around his waist once he was comfortably in place, tugging Mydei back to lean against him. “What?”

“Asset?” 

Phainon’s mouth parted with realisation, which spread into a grin as he lifted one arm and flexed. “These. Obviously.” 

Mydei hummed, considering, and then darted forward and left a kiss on his bicep. Phainon startled back with a garbled sound but Mydei laughed. “You were so petty earlier, yet retreat when I give the affection you asked for.”

“Wha—“ Phainon sputtered. “You surprised me. Go again. I’m prepared this time.”

He twisted back around and sank lower into the water. It was pleasantly warm, yet was almost chilly in comparison to the earlier heat. “No.”

“Mydei,” he whined like a deprived dog. Then added, “Later?” 

“Perhaps,” he said haughtily, as though he could ever truly deny Phainon. Even those kisses he had demanded would be his to receive later when Mydei’s lips had fully healed. 

The silence settled between them with the still waters. Peaceful, if not for Phainon’s thumbs rubbing slow circles at Mydei’s hips. he watched Phainon’s toes curl beneath the water. Thoughtful. Fidgeting. Nervous. 

“My hatred.” 

Mydei didn’t look at him. Didn’t acknowledge his words beyond his hands set upon Phainon’s own in a reassuring, grounding touch. 

Phainon laughed under his breath, warm against the shell of Mydei’s ear, and dropped his head against Mydei’s shoulder. “My most valuable… I couldn’t have survived without it.” 

Eyes closed, Mydei tilted his face into Phainon’s bared neck, smelling a hyacinths on a humid day. “You don’t possess one.”

“Oh,” he attempted to keep his voice level rather than wounded as it rumbled against Mydei’s nose against his throat “All right…”

“There is no best nor worst. There’s only you, and nothing about you I would pick or choose.”

“All right…” Phainon said, forcibly even despite them both feeling his chest stammer against Mydei’s back. 

He tipped his head, revealing his smirk to Phainon’s flushed face. “Not what you expected?”

Phainon’s face twisted with displeasure but he couldn’t deny it. “How could anyone expect that. I’m just a man, Mydei. You need to stop with the romantic lines. What happened to ‘romance does not exist in the Kremnoan language’?” Phainon recounted with a poor imitation of Mydei’s usual gruffness. “Was that a lie so you could murder me with a heart attack? Cuteness aggression?”

He straightened his head and closed his eyes to enjoy the water in full. “I never lie.”

He expected another witty retort, more whining, or an attempt to quash Mydei’s apparent “romanticisms”—they were nothing of the sort. They were simply the truths he wished to tell; the same as all his words. Those were the only ones worth speaking—with Phainon’s own. Nothing.

But Phainon’s arms tightened around him and he nuzzled against Myde’s temple. “I know.”

I know he said in the same tone as—

Mydei leaned his ear against Phainon’s chest. Whether it was a heart beating hot, a thrumming golden brilliance, a flickering pale flame, they all pulsed to the same rhythm. Lit by hatred upon a tinder of love that kept the fire burning bright over the horizon. 

I love you that irradiant core meant to fulfil their wishes had told his fallen allies. 

I love you that dying flame kept safeguarded just long enough to succeed told Amphoreus. 

I love you that beating heart told Mydei.

“I know,” Mydei answered them all.

chapters.html:
End Notes

Mini-rant about love and hatred in Amphoreus

So I know Phainon and Cyrene are supposed to represent hatred and love respectively, hence Neikos and Philia being their names.

BUT, to me, Phainon represents both hatred and love. Whether he hates Flame Reaver, Lygus, Nanook or fate itself, it’s because they harm/threaten to harm his loved ones. All of his overwhelming hatred stems from the fact he loves everyone so much.

His wish as a child was to make other people’s wishes come true because he knows how to love others better than himself.

Phainon just exudes love. Hatred alone would never have been enough for the original Phainon and every Phainon after that to make the decision to enter the Eternal Recurrences, or to sustain him through them.

To Phainon, his hatred (in a negative, derisive kind of way) was the most important. But Mydei can recognise that it was the love that allowed his hatred to burn.

Hoyo can pry Smolrene from my cold dead corpse. Where are her poofy sleeves and moon sceptre.
